findings.issue: A behavior change that hits default runs is in no changelog. The review graph upsert now adds one FINDING node and one EVIDENCE_FOR edge for each finding that has a path:line ref (deriveReviewFindingEvidence). It also folds prefixed leaf finding ids onto the stored node (resolveReviewFindingId). For every loop type, an edge to an undeclared node is now skipped and listed in rejectedOrphanEdges, where the whole batch used to roll back. Commit 7c6a2d9a7e5 says 'This changes default runs': before it, a review graph whose leaf sent no evidence edges could never allow a stop. None of hub v2.1.0.0-v2.1.7.0, runtime v1.10.0.0, deep-review v1.11.18.0/v1.12.0.0/v1.13.0.0 or deep-research v1.16.0.0 mentions it. Only runtime/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md:620 describes it.

evidence.cmd: grep -rn -iE 'orphan|undeclared|rejectedOrphan|finding node|density|EVIDENCE_FOR|evidence.?edge' changelog/v2.1.*.md runtime/changelog/v1.10.0.0.md deep-review/changelog/v1.1[123]*.md deep-research/changelog/v1.16.0.0.md

findings.issue: No open root release note describes what this scope adds. The newest root entry is v4.1.0.0, and a v4.1.0.0 tag already exists that is not an ancestor of HEAD. Under sk-create-changelog SKILL.md section 8, step 196-198, a tagged highest entry is closed, so new work needs a new numbered entry. The entry has no mention of --depth-mode=expansive, the frontier, --extend/--extend-minutes, custom review dimensions or the review minimum-iteration floor, but the root README (lines 253-255) and the skill changelogs describe all of these. The S6-release-coverage battery passed only because it checks that the component id system-deep-loop appears, not that these capabilities are covered.
